findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: There is a drain in the seafood department that is not draining any waste water. The PIC of this department stated that they squeegee the water to another drain due to the drain not draining. The PIC also stated that they have not noticed any sewage backing up. There has been a ticket put in for this issue, but the issue has not yet been repaired. A follow up is scheduled for 1/13/2026 (allows the store another day to get a company to come repair the drain) to ensure that the drain has been fixed and is sufficiently allowing waste water to drain.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: Observed two bags of cooked chicken in cooler in deli to not be marked with a prepared/use by date. Bags of chicken were labeled with today’s date. (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing solution in sanitizer bucket in meat department to test at 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. Bucket that tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia made upon request.  4-501.114 Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. 
A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under ¶4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, P and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: 
(1) Have a minimum temperature of 24oC (75oF), P

(3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions;P

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) The facility has an infrared thermometer that they use to take temperatures. While this is an excellent monitoring tool, a stem thermometer should be available for monitoring the internal temps of foods. ALSO, the digital display one the cheese display deli cooler is not working and the adjacent meat display is reading 54F. This is not accuate.  All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820b  A temporary drainboad/rolling cart is being set beneath the papertoweling dispenser of the deli handsink. This results in wet hands dripping across a clean drying surface/clean dishes. No dishes were present during the inspection. The drainboard should be pulled away from the paper towels so cross-contamination is not a potential. Drain boards and/or dish tables shall be provided for proper handling of soiled utensils prior to washing and clean utensils following sanitizing and shall be located as to not interfere with the proper use of other facilities.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed multiple potentially hazardous foods items in the south-east display cooler not being maintained at 41F or below. Multiple items at 42-45F. Refrigeration service provider is on site to repair the unit. Do not re-stock this display cooler until a spot check in conducted on Monday to ensure all potentially hazardous food items are being maintained at 41F or below. See General Comments for additional details.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Display coolers around the deli do not have thermometers provided in the warmest parts of the coolers. Provide thermometers in the warmest part of the coolers to ensure all potentially hazardous foods will be maintained at 41F or below. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Each mechanically refrigerated storage facility storing potentially hazardous foods shall be provided with a numerically scaled indicating thermometer, accurate to plus or minus 3 degrees F., located to measure the air temperature in the warmest of the facility and located to be easily readable.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a knife and cutting board to be soiled with food debris and left unattended. If cutting boards and knives are to be used on a continual basis, ensure food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least once every four hours to prevent possible pathogen growth.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
One sandwich wrap and one burrito were found at temperatures of 45 degrees F and 46 degrees F, respectively (taken with probe thermometer).  CORRECTED - both items were immediately, voluntarily discarded.  Initially, air thermometer on Sandwiches case read 50 degrees F.  Within ~10 minutes, air thermometer read 32 degrees F, and ~10 minutes later it had jumped up to 46 degrees F.  Staff should closely monitor case for proper cold holding temperatures, as well as possibility of faulty air thermometer (digital, at back left side of case).
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Upon start of inspection, deli manager stated that hot holding for fried chicken, fried fish, etc. has not been working, and staff has been changing out food every hour or so.  While staff appear to be taking temperatures and recording them on clipboard every hour, the time the food was taken out of proper cooking is not recorded.  It appears staff is attempting to memorize the times for all the foods.  Deli manager says that proper cooking temperature is confirmed before food is taken for hot holding.  Also, hot holding cabinet in back kitchen does not appear to be holding all foods >135 degrees F.  CORRECTED - 2nd shift deli manager immediately drew a map of the hot holding and recorded the times that each food was taken from cooking equipment.  She also labeled the pan of fried chicken in the back kitchen hot holding cabinet.  Time as a Control was thoroughly discussed with both deli managers, and store manager, and a policy form was left with deli manager.
750-153(a) When using time as a control, food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135°F or above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following food-contact surfaces are soiled:
(a) lower fryer panel, on far right fryer in kitchen (soiled w/ grease accumulation (REPEAT x3)), 
(b)  lower fryer panel on left fryer (grease accumulation) (REPEAT), 
(c) transporter cabinet (inside soiled).  
Discussed cleaning routine w/ staff.  It appears that 2x/yr, all staff thoroughly detail clean throughout store (including fryers).  In the meantime, staff is supposed to work on cleaning fryers in down time.  Discussed increasing the frequency with which the lower fryer panels are cleaned, as they continuously show signs of grease accumulation.  Clean the aforementioned surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
The three lower shelves of clean equipment were soiled with food debris, flour, etc.  The rolling trash can was rolled up against the shelving unit, and it appears that discarded items were being splashed onto the clean equipment shelves.  CORRECTED - staff immediately took all pans of utensils and equipment into dish room for wash, rinse, sanitize.  Store sanitized equipment in a way that protects them from contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:

750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
The spicy breading bulk container in the kitchen had no label as to its contents (REPEAT x2).  Staff state labels constantly fall off.  Large square container of breading mix stored under prep table is also unlabeled.  Label container as to its contents (consider writing on container with permanent marker).
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: 14 whole rottisserie chickens found at temperatures of 108, 112, 114, 166, 118 degrees F (tested with probe thermometer).  Staff states they were removed from rottisserie at 8:30 am, which was the last time their temperatures had been monitored.  (Minutes later, a staff member discovers that the lower hot plate had not been turned on).  Any chickens remaining at 12:30pm (not sold) will be discarded.  See Voluntary Destruction Form.     750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

750-1120c Sinks used for food preparation or for washing equipment or utensils shall not be used for hand washing.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.150 - Hot case holding rotisserie chickens was not hot to the touch. Surface temperature was 86F according to inspector's infrared thermometer. Employee that placed the chickens in the display forgot to turn on the case. Once the case was turned on the surface temperature increased. Temperatures for chickens were still above 135F. Turn on the hot cases prior to placing cooked products inside to ensure proper hot holding temperature will be maintained at all times. It is a bad practice to turn on hot and cold holding units immediately before the are in use. All units used to store potentially hazardous foods need to be in proper working order before placing products in them.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Large slicer was stored between the counter and knife holder in the cheese prep area. The slicer was soiled with what appeared to be old cheese debris and the crevice where it was stored had similar chunks of debris stuck in it. Clean and sanitized equipment shall be stored in a manner that protects items from potential cross contamination. The slicer was taken to dish area for proper wash, rinse, and sanitize. Do not store slicers, knives, and other utensils in crevices or other areas that can not be maintained in a sanitary condition.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact

B) Powdered sugar and flour bins in bakery had plastic cups as scoops. Cups did not have handles. Use scoops with handles for dispensing all foods, and store scoops with handles extended up out of foods between uses.
